dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Stay on your guard, citizen!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Me? As you can see, I'm busy dealing with the barbarian threat! According to the reports I've received, there've been traces of them skulking about here.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: This is no trivial matter! Vigilance must be maintained until reinforcements arrive!

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: If there is anything else, please bring it up with my adjutant, citizen.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A child, out here on their own...

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Hmm? A child? Where from? Did some new legionnaire disobey orders and bring their family into the camp again...?

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: *sigh* Dominus Cassiodor is far too gentle with these greenhorns. If this were to have happened three decades prior, a Tribunus would've had a whip out by now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have there been any suspicious happenings lately?

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Not at present. That said, the barbarians are akin to cunning beasts. Ever will they strike when your guard has been lowered, for surprise is their greatest weapon!

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: By methods most foul they infiltrate our cities and seek out our secrets. Even the slightest lapse in discipline may lead to catastrophe.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: *sigh* Thirty years ago, when I followed Dominus Boethius to conquest in the far north, they were but a pack of primitives without any such skill for subterfuge. Where did they learn these tricks?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Fare ye well, citizen! You may report suspicious people to me at any time!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thirty years ago... Your parents wouldn't even have been born yet...

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Hmm? What did you just say, citizen? I fear my hearing's been going as I age.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: *sigh* Time truly is cruel. During the conquest of Bituria, I could hear the barbarians' bells calling them to muster from miles away.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is soooo boring. My dream was more interesting than life here. I wanna go see the outside world!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What sort of dream would be that interesting?

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: A very, very long one! Uh, I don't really remember much of it anymore, though. Did I have it yesterday? Or have I had it before...

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: I dreamed that the town was invaded, and I joined up with the Gardes, becoming an awesome officer — even my dad had to listen to me!

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: I would say, "Giovanni, bring me my gun," and he could only say, "Sir, yes, sir!"

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: In the past, when I would dream, I would wake up once I realized that something didn't add up. But that dream was perfect. I was so happy, I could've played in there forever.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: I guess it's because of my recent desire to go on an adventure.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is Petrichor that boring?

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Exactly! Nothing ever changes around here, and everyone's okay with that... If it wasn't like this, Uncle would never have left!

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: I wanted to go see the outside world... I heard people in town say that Sumeru's an interesting place, with its rainforests and deserts... and ancient fortresses and temples!

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Here, it's all water everywhere you look... Ah, how I wish I could go on an adventure!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The outside world isn't that interesting either.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Eh? Wouldn't you have had to see every kind of other place before you can say that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your uncle?

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: That's right. I don't know his name, and he's never written us any letters... Dad always calls him "that blockhead," or "that guy"...

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: But he's gotta be a pretty awesome guy to have bucked with tradition and left town by himself to Sumeru! Better than Dad, who only ever talks about family and duty and stuff like that...

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Uh, hmm. Did I say too much? Keep that stuff a secret and don't tell Dad, alright? Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your uncle?

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: That's right! My uncle was in Sumeru before, but he came back in the last couple of days.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: Dad says that Uncle didn't get anything done other than get himself into a bunch of debt before returning, but I bet that's a lie.

dialogues.speaker: Moce
dialogues.text: He just said that because he doesn't want me to leave town!
